stories.body: Iran says the US response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz is unconvincing, while President Donald Trump has confirmed a US strike on an Iranian anti-aircraft facility. Iranian media said the strike hit Qeshm Island near the waterway. Qatar says it is facilitating an exchange of proposals and that both sides remain committed to negotiations. Iran’s demands include lifting sanctions and ending a US naval blockade.
stories.headline: Iran rejects US response to Hormuz proposal as Trump confirms strikes

stories.body: South Africans are voting in municipal elections amid frustration over water outages, power cuts, corruption and deteriorating infrastructure. Polls suggest the African National Congress could fall below a third of the vote, down from 45.6% in the 2021 local elections. Fragmented support could produce more coalition governments in cities where frequent changes of leadership have already complicated service delivery.
stories.headline: South Africans vote in local elections amid anger over failing services

stories.body: Bomb threats prompted searches or diversions involving at least seven passenger flights across Europe on Tuesday. All landed safely and no explosives were found. Warsaw’s Modlin airport briefly closed, and Italian fighter jets escorted a Ryanair flight from Dublin into Rome. Authorities were investigating whether the threats were connected; officials reported no immediate evidence of a hostile state or terrorist activity.
stories.headline: Bomb threats disrupt seven flights across Europe

stories.body: Greenland’s parliament voted 16–0, with seven abstentions, to approve a security agreement with the US and Denmark. The deal allows for expanded US military activity, including at Pituffik Space Base, and followed months of tension over Donald Trump’s threats to seize the island. Danish lawmakers are due to debate the agreement later this month; it will enter into force after the necessary parliamentary processes in the Danish kingdom are complete.
stories.headline: Greenland’s parliament approves security deal with the US and Denmark

stories.body: Brazil has published a global roadmap intended to help countries move away from coal, oil and gas, ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. The document grew out of a compromise at last year’s COP30 talks and is intended to guide implementation by government ministries. Climate scientist Joeri Rogelj welcomed it as a step forward but said it lacked a timeline and benchmarks for the pace of change.
stories.headline: Brazil publishes global roadmap for moving away from fossil fuels

stories.body: Democrats have won control of the Senate and the House in the midterm elections, ending Republican control of both chambers. The Associated Press projected that Democrats secured at least 51 Senate seats, with some races still being counted. Democratic gains included seats in Texas, Ohio, Kansas and the Carolinas, delivering a major setback to President Donald Trump’s party.
stories.headline: Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress

stories.body: James Talarico won the Texas Senate race and Gina Hinojosa won the governorship, giving Democrats their first victories in either office in more than a generation. Talarico defeated Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, while Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott. Democrats also led in other statewide contests as counting continued, with strong results in urban areas and a reversal of recent Republican gains in the Rio Grande Valley.
stories.headline: Democrats win Texas Senate and governor races

stories.body: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, a former Atlanta mayor and adviser to Joe Biden, won Georgia’s governor race against Republican Rick Jackson, according to an Associated Press projection. Her victory makes her the first Black woman elected governor of a US state. Jackson spent more than $200 million of his own money in the race to succeed term-limited Republican Governor Brian Kemp.
stories.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes first Black woman elected governor of a US state

stories.body: Óscar Puente resigned as transport minister after two serious high-speed rail crashes in less than a year, including the collision near Urda that killed 69 people last week. Announcing his decision before lawmakers, he said a minister could not remain in office after two such disasters. He also withdrew from the Socialist Party’s list for the November 29 general election. Earlier, he announced safety measures including a second operator’s confirmation for decisions made when automatic safety systems are down.
stories.headline: Transport minister Óscar Puente resigns after two deadly train crashes

stories.body: Worker representatives at rail infrastructure manager Adif have agreed to a November 17 strike over safety concerns and have proposed a joint stoppage with Renfe workers. Union sources said the strike had not yet been formally called and arrangements at Renfe were still being finalized. A demonstration is planned outside Congress on November 16. Separately, the train drivers’ union Semaf has called strikes for November 10 and 12.
stories.headline: Adif and Renfe workers plan November 17 strike over rail safety

stories.body: Supreme Court judge Pablo Llarena has closed the investigative stage of the case against former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont and former ministers Toni Comín and Lluís Puig over the 2017 independence bid. He sent the case to the court’s criminal chamber, which must decide whether to dismiss it under the amnesty law. Arrest warrants against the three had already been lifted, allowing Puigdemont to return to Spain.
stories.headline: Judge closes investigation of Puigdemont and two former ministers, paving way for amnesty

stories.body: Negotiators have reached a preliminary agreement on a limited joint declaration for the Ibero-American summit in Madrid, subject to approval by the heads of the 22 delegations. Spain secured the draft despite ideological divisions and the absence of several leaders, including Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexico’s Claudia Sheinbaum. The previous summit in Ecuador ended without a final declaration.
stories.headline: Ibero-American summit negotiators reach preliminary agreement on limited declaration

stories.body: A Barcelona judge ordered an 18-year-old held without bail over his alleged role in organising violent unrest through the Blocus network. The judge said messages and instructions in online groups pointed to a possible leadership role; the man denied responsibility. In a separate case, a judge ordered another alleged Blocus leader held without bail, citing evidence from seized devices and concerns about flight and further offences.
stories.headline: Judge orders alleged Barcelona unrest organiser held without bail

stories.body: Catalan writer Cristina Fernández Cubas has won the Cervantes Prize, the Spanish-speaking world’s most prestigious official literary award. The jury praised her originality and her contribution to the contemporary short story and fantastic literature. Born in Arenys de Mar in 1945 and a Barcelona resident, she published her first story collection, Mi hermana Elba, in 1980 and has since written fiction, memoir and essays.
stories.headline: Cristina Fernández Cubas wins the 2026 Cervantes Prize

stories.body: Protesters camped in Plaça de Catalunya for the right to housing say they intend to stay until after Spain’s November 29 general election. Around 30 people gathered in the square on Tuesday to condemn the eviction of a similar camp in Madrid’s Puerta del Sol. Barcelona organisers said they were concerned about further evictions but had not received notice to leave.
stories.headline: Barcelona housing protesters plan to remain in Plaça de Catalunya through the election

stories.body: The Spanish government has provisionally allocated €3.9 million to renovate the monastery in Sant Feliu de Guíxols that will house a future Thyssen museum. The museum will display Catalan paintings from the baroness’s collection and is expected to open in mid-2028. The town has put the first phase of renovation out to tender, with work expected to begin around the end of this year or the start of 2027.
stories.headline: Spain allocates €3.9 million to future Thyssen museum in Sant Feliu de Guíxols
